purpose: Test whether foreground/background-conditioned channel weighting of the existing SAM2 early feature contrast improves identification of useful Lean memory tokens under the same fixed budget.
source: Uses the author ChannelGate class from external/TCMN/model/cbam.py (itself adapted from the official CBAM implementation). The experiment uses only that channel gate and does not reproduce TCMN, full CBAM, or a trained channel-to-channel transformer.
method: From the initial automatic mask construct the existing SAM2 early-FPN foreground and background prototypes. Feed the pair [foreground, negative background] into the author's average/max-pooling channel gate. Multiply the same channel weights into each current/source early feature and into both prototypes before normalizing and computing the existing foreground-minus-background cosine contrast. Store the resulting 64x64 scores aligned with original token IDs through the existing observer; no GT, later detector pass or new confidence threshold enters inference.
checkpoint_policy: A compatible 32-channel checkpoint is not currently available. Inference requires an explicit strict checkpoint with author CBAM source hash, exact SAM2 backbone checkpoint hash, fixed FPN interface, feature-pipeline hash, positive declared training steps and a hashed training manifest. The caller must derive the pipeline identity from its loaded runtime, including bypass and preprocessing. These fields help detect mismatches; they do not by themselves prove training, actual runtime identity, or absence of leakage. Nonfinite parameters are rejected. An initialized gate without checkpoint may run only in explicit training mode with gradients enabled.
validation_done: Unit checks cover the author gate, gradients, invalid weights, feature-pipeline/checkpoint contract, inference/no-grad guard, exact score-to-token alignment and hook restoration on success and error. Two independent label-free real-feature checks use zeroed gate weights in gradient-enabled engineering mode to give uniform channel weights and compare against existing unweighted contrast; the archived prompt is pinned by two prompt-gate receipts. No learnt inference or segmentation-quality claim is made.
next_work: Before any efficacy run define and audit patient/sequence-independent training and validation data, keep the prioritized evaluation sequences out of training, capture automatic-prompt features with input and model hashes, train and verify a checkpoint with comparable training allowance for controls. Compare unweighted early-FPN contrast, trained channel weighting, RGB, shuffled-channel and usage/distributed controls at identical frames, eligible tokens and attention-key counts. Test full propagation only if frozen same-state diagnostics justify it. Track empty-frame false alarms separately.
limits: Uniform-weight no-op checks prove interface equivalence only; fabricated metadata can falsely claim training, so audited training artifacts are required. The initial automatic mask may be a distractor and can contaminate both region descriptors. The score is attention-weighted cosine, not an independent measurement of causal utility. No inference-time threshold, gating or redetection is introduced.
